description: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70.
title: Barry Melrose, former NHL player-turned-coach and broadcaster, dead at 70

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: There is a more than 10 per cent chance that AI could kill all humans within the next decade, a researcher at Anthropic estimated in a post, hours after social media posts went viral from someone saying they had just quit Anthropic over concerns that AI companies are “gambling with our lives” in the AI development race.
title: AI researchers 'earnestly believe' it could kill all humans within the next decade, Anthropic researcher says

author: Sarah Petz
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in Canada this week for his first visit to the country in nearly a year as his country copes with an onslaught of deadly airstrikes.
title: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visits Canada
Apple's new iPhone Duo costs more in Canada, but not because of tariffs

description: One of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that careened off a Miami runway and killed five people repeatedly warned they were coming in too fast nearly two minutes ahead of time and at the last second urged them to abort the landing, according to highlights of the cockpit recording that investigators released Wednesday.
title: Pilot of Amazon plane flagged excessive speed before deadly Miami crash, investigators say

author: Meagan Fitzpatrick
description: The personal information of people involved in Ontario's court systems may have been stolen in a cyber attack, according to the chief justices of the province. An online case management system used by the courts and owned by Thomson Reuters Canada Limited was breached in June.
title: Ontario courts warn personal information may have been exposed in cyberattack

author: Wallis Snowdon
description: Surveillance video showing a former detainee being released from a corrections transport van into the streets of Edmonton’s Chinatown has raised concerns over how Alberta offenders are released into the community.
title: Release of detainee into Chinatown parking lot prompts anger, calls for reform in Edmonton

author: Abby Hughes
description: With some tariffs added and others removed, economists predict that big picture the changes will break even. But certain industries will still be hit hard, they say, and the tit-for-tat will weigh on business owners' confidence.
title: What will Trump's retaliatory tariffs do to Canada’s economy big picture? Not that much, economists predict

author: Conrad Collaco
description: Amid a trade war that includes President Donald Trump's threats to Canadian sovereignty and his vow to ban imports of several Canadian products to the U.S., the NFL's Buffalo Bills have made an unexpected announcement.
title: Buffalo Bills to 'celebrate' O Canada at home opener amid more Trump threats during trade war

description: A B.C. family doctor has been ordered to pay $28,100, after refusing to inject a transgender teen with a prescribed hormone blocker, citing religious and cultural reasons.
title: Human Rights Tribunal orders B.C. doctor to pay after refusing to provide trans teen with puberty blocker shot

author: Darren Major
description: The federal government is moving ahead with changes that will exempt a number of energy projects from a layer of its environmental assessment process.
title: Government exempts interprovincial pipelines from review by impact assessment agency

description: Noel Clarke, best known for his role in the sci-fi show Doctor Who from 2005 to 2010, has been charged with six sexual offences, including two counts of sexual assault, England and Wales’ Crown Prosecution Service announced on Wednesday.
title: Ex-Doctor Who actor Noel Clarke charged with several sexual offences including assault, voyeurism

description: On Sept. 11, 2001, thousands of unexpected guests arrived in Gander, N.L. and nearby towns when terrorist attacks shut down airspace over North America. For The National, CBC’s David Common revisits the community’s extraordinary response on the day ‘the plane people’ arrived and the enduring bonds that remain 25 years later.
title: How Gander, N.L., took care of ‘the plane people’ on 9/11

author: Anchal Sharma
description: Guy Turcotte was sentenced to life in prison in 2015 after being convicted of second-degree murder in the stabbing deaths of his two young children.
title: Guy Turcotte, who killed his 2 children, requesting temporary absence from prison

author: Kayla McLean
description: South Park appears to be taking a page out of Donald Trump's book: if you don’t like a name, change it. For its 29th season, the animated satire has announced a new title — and will be now known as South America.
title: South Park pulls a Trump, to be renamed South America for new season

author: Alina Snisarenko
description: An Ontario man was found guilty of participating in the activities of a terrorist group by an Ontario Superior Court judge Wednesday.
title: Ontario man found guilty of terrorism charge related to neo-Nazi group

author: Dylan Robertson
description: As the Carney government pursues deeper relations with Beijing, the Chinese government reports it held a "candid" exchange on military issues with Canadian officials earlier this month.
title: China says it held 'candid and in-depth' military talks with Canadian officials last week

author: Ruma Paul
description: Bangladesh, which once came close to eliminating measles, is facing its worst outbreak on record, with around 1,000 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since March as hospitals struggle with overcrowding, shortages and a continuing influx of sick children.
title: Bangladesh in grips of world's worst measles outbreak, with 1,000 dead in last 6 months

description: The Edmonton Oilers have signed forward Alex Formenton to a one-year contract worth $850,000 US.
title: Acquitted world junior player Alex Formenton signs one-year deal with Edmonton Oilers

description: A monthly report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation says the August number marks the steepest year-over-year drop since March.
title: Average asking rents fall 4.8% in August as trade war adds fresh uncertainty: report

description: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to ‌deliver relief to displaced people.
title: Drones a key part of Nepal's response to flash-flood disaster

description: A Quebec judge has found rapper K'naan not guilty of sexually assaulting a woman while she slept in his Quebec City hotel room in 2010.
title: Quebec judge finds rapper K'naan not guilty in sexual assault trial

description: Apple is widely expected to unveil a pricey folding iPhone at a launch event on Wednesday at its Cupertino, Calif., headquarters.
title: Apple expected to unveil pricey folding iPhone in its 1st major overhaul in a decade

author: Emily Chung
description: Fossil eggshells believed to be from some of the biggest dinosaurs that ever lived have been found in a surprisingly cool climate far from the equator. But those titanosaurs were too big to sit on their eggs. Microscopic evidence shows what they did instead to keep the eggs warm enough to hatch.
title: The biggest dinosaurs couldn't sit on their eggs. Scientists say they did this instead

description: Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, with the attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sending the international Brent crude benchmark over $100 US a barrel for the first time since July.
title: Renewed U.S.-Iran exchanges send oil price back over $100 US for first time in several weeks

author: Halyna Mihalik
description: Schools in northern Saskatchewan are adapting to prepare students to work in a mine that's under construction in the region. It's an unprecedented economic opportunity, but it doesn't come without concerns for the environment.
title: How are northern Sask. schools preparing youth for new mining opportunities?

author: Emily Fagan
description: CBC News has spent months going through court records and speaking with victims in the largest case of voyeurism ever reported in Canada. Victims say it has left them feeling shattered, hunted and struggling to continue on with their normal lives.
title: 'Hunted,' 'shattered,' 'scared': How victims say Canada's most prolific voyeur has altered their lives

description: Ben Shelton had gone toe-to-toe with Carlos Alcaraz for five exhausting sets and finally, at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday, came the chance to end the U.S. Open champion's title reign.
title: Ben Shelton beats defending champ Carlos Alcaraz in U.S. Open match that ends after 3:30 a.m.

author: Murray Brewster, Daniel Leblanc
description: Ottawa moved to acquire six GlobalEye surveillance aircraft without assurances they met military requirements — requirements not shared with competing manufacturers. Subsequent assessments identified capability gaps requiring modifications, raising questions about whether the Carney government’s push for speed, jobs and industrial benefits is taking precedence over the military’s operational needs.
title: GlobalEye gamble: Ottawa chose surveillance plane without knowing it met military needs

author: Hénia Ould-Hammou
description: Sixteen police officers are under investigation over racist acts targeting Black and Arab people. Two historians explain how the alleged cutting and collecting of locs connects to a history of slavery, racism and control over Black bodies.
title: Montreal police allegedly cut locs from people's hair. Here's the anti-Black history behind that

author: Kevin Maimann
description: Art crime experts say last year's headline-grabbing Louvre heist seems to have inspired a rash of brazen art thefts, putting European museums holding valuable art in a tough spot. Thieves cut a hole in a fence and climbed through a window to steal four paintings from the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera early Tuesday, local authorities said.
title: Recent art thefts appear to be inspired by 2025 Louvre heist, art crime experts say

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: Amid the buzz surrounding the upcoming Toronto International Film Festival, U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed the creation of a federal tax incentive to keep film production in the U.S. instead of seeing it move to other countries – calling out Canada by name. But is it fair to frame the Hollywood exodus as Canada taking jobs from the U.S.?
title: The U.S. is considering a federal tax incentive for films. How might that affect Canada?

author: Nick Logan
description: A group of Calgary parents is sharing their stories and concerns about the danger of carbon monoxide inside hockey arenas, after their own children were exposed to high levels of the odourless gas during a weekend tournament nearly two years ago.
title: Their kids were exposed to carbon monoxide at a hockey rink. They're trying to prevent it from happening again

author: Eric Szeto, Jeff Yates, Christian Paas-Lang, Jordan Pearson, Ivan Angelovski
description: An investigation by CBC's visual investigations team and Radio-Canada's Décrypteurs has discovered a Vietnamese company is linked to a network of Facebook pages and websites sharing misleading, sensationalist or outright false news headlines.
title: Vietnamese firm targets Canadians with fake AI news for profit, CBC/Rad-Can investigation reveals

description: An investigation by CBC's visual investigations team and Radio-Canada's Décrypteurs has discovered a Vietnamese company is linked to a network of Facebook pages and websites sharing misleading, sensationalist or outright false news headlines.
title: Vietnamese firm targets Canadians with fake AI news for profit, CBC/Radio-Canada investigation reveals
